Kocsord Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dankó Pista utca 2, Hungary

Demolished. By 1828, Kocsord already had 47 Jewish residents; the population reached 73 by 1880 and 60 by 1941. This cemetery was possibly founded after 1891, since it does not appear on that year's cadastral map, and was destroyed at an unknown time, most likely during or soon after WWII. According to local resident Nagy Elek, the individual responsible for demolishing the cemetery was later tried and sentenced to prison. The Jewish inhabitants of Kocsord were deported from the Mátészalka Ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, on May 25, 1944.
